declared.title: Income and emotional well-being: Evidence for well-being plateauing around $200,000 per year
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « income and emotional well-being a conflict resolved adversarial collaboration » (2026-11-22)

population: household income and emotional well-being; the data used are not named in the abstract (full text not read)

findings.text: With the threshold estimated from the data, emotional well-being stops rising only above about $200,000 a year

support.sentence: Using a data-driven approach to detect the placement of the threshold, we find a flat relationship between household income and emotional well-being above a threshold around $200,000 per year.

findings.text: The author concludes that the evidence is not yet enough for definite conclusions

support.sentence: We conclude that although the analysis of this paper provides some evidence for well-being plateauing around $200,000 per year, more research is needed before any definite conclusions about the relationship between emotional well-being and income can be drawn.

limits: a short letter; the author lists the assumptions it relies on
cross-sectional: an association, not an effect of money
data source and sample not checked (full text not read)
